_readme: The in-game Field Guide (J, or Pause > Field Guide). Edit the text here; numbers (HP, damage, prices...) are filled in from the game data automatically. Add an entry under a section using the thing's id. 'lore' is a short paragraph, 'tips' is a list of one-liners.

revolver.lore: A trusty six-shooter. Accurate, quick to reload, and every rancher's first friend.
tips: Aim (right mouse) for a tighter, zoomed shot.
Glowing weak spots take double damage.

lever_rifle.lore: A long gun that punches clean through beetle shell. Slow to cycle, but nothing laughs it off.
tips: Pierces armour: your answer to Rattler Beetles.
Zooms 2.2x when aimed.

coach_shotgun.lore: Two barrels of buckshot for when the bugs are already on the porch.
tips: Aiming tightens the spread.
Useless at range, brutal up close.

blunderbuss.lore: A bell-mouthed flintlock that throws a fistful of nails and shot.
tips: One shot, then a slow muzzle-load: make it count.
Brutal against anything that reaches your plateau.

crank_gatling.lore: A six-barrel gatling you crank by hand, with a drum on top.
tips: Hold fire: it winds up for a moment, then keeps firing.
Sixty rounds a drum; swapping drums takes a few seconds.

derringer_pair.lore: A gambler's pair of hideout pistols, one per hand. They clear leather before anything else you own and empty in a blink.
tips: Click fast: right hand, left hand, right, left.
Damage drops off hard past a few metres: it's for the spider already on the porch.
Reloads both in under a second.

pepperbox.lore: Six barrels drilled into one turning block. Nobody ever hit what they aimed at with one, but up close it hardly matters.
tips: Fast and wild: get close, then hold your nerve and keep clicking.
All six reload at once.

salt_shotgun.lore: Rock salt instead of buckshot: the farmer's way to say "get off my land". It stings so much the bugs forget to hold on.
tips: Every climber you hit slides a few metres back down the wall.
Big bugs slide less; bosses barely budge, and not twice in a row.
Useless for killing: pair it with turrets that hit hard.

harpoon_pistol.lore: A spring-gun that throws a barbed whaling dart on a line. What happens next depends on who's heavier.
tips: Small bugs get reeled in to your feet, or yanked off the wall to fall.
Big bugs, bosses and rock pull YOU to them, like the grapple.
Jump to let go of the line early.

bee_smoker.lore: Any beekeeper knows smoke calms a hive. It turns out it calms a spider the size of a mule just as well.
tips: Hold fire to puff: fliers and spiders in the cloud go drowsy and slow right down.
Drowsy fliers sink low enough to swat.
Does no damage, and the burlap refills itself when you stop.

flare_gun.lore: Meant for calling the cavalry. Out here it calls every turret on both cliffs to the same bug.
tips: Hit a bug and it burns red for six seconds: all turrets shoot it first.
Fire it at the rock or the sky at night to light the canyon.
One shot, then a slow reload: pick your target.

punt_gun.lore: Built to bring down a whole flock of ducks from a punt. Somebody sawed it short and now shoots it from the hip.
tips: One huge cone of shot: perfect for a pack at the lip.
The kick shoves you back a few steps. Mind the edge.
A long reload: switch guns rather than wait.

telescope_rifle.lore: A target rifle with a brass spyglass strapped on top. Patient, precise and murderous on a weak spot.
tips: Right click to look down the spyglass.
Weak spots take five times the damage.
Work the bolt between shots: make every one count.

dust_mite.lore: Rust-red scuttlers that come in clouds. One shot each, but there are always more.
tips: Gatling Posts and Chili Mortars eat swarms.
Never let a pack reach the lip unchallenged.

wolf_spider.lore: Fast, long-legged hunters that leap up the rock in bounds.
tips: Lasso Harpoons pin them mid-climb.
Watch for sudden leaps near the top.

rattler_beetle.lore: Teal tanks with a front shell that shrugs off small arms.
tips: Hit them from above or behind, where the shell is thin.
Buffalo Rifles and the lever-action pierce the shell.

spitter_scorpion.lore: Clings halfway up and spits acid at your turrets.
tips: Turrets on scaffolding can see further down.
They give up and climb after a while.

brood_mother.lore: A bloated spider carrying a living cargo of spiderlings.
tips: Hit her hard and fast: the brood bursts out at half health.
Splash turrets clean up the spiderlings.

spiderling.lore: A brood mother's children. Tiny, quick and many.
tips: Mortars and repeaters handle them fine.

burrow_tick.lore: Digs under the plateau and surfaces among your crops.
tips: Keep a gun handy near the farm.
House turrets cover the yard.

dragonfly_bandit.lore: Flies straight over the canyon and snatches what it can.
tips: Shoot them down yourself or with plateau guards.
They ignore cliff-face turrets.

crop_weevil.lore: Heads for your farm plots and chews them bare.
tips: Weevils pay walls no mind: they head straight for the crops.
Bear traps on the approach help.

iron_tumble.lore: The boss: a giant silver rhinoceros beetle with a horn like a church steeple and a tumbleweed stuck on its back. It comes on the last wave and rams the house when it reaches the top.
tips: Turrets across the canyon hit its back as it climbs.
Shoot its glowing belly from above.

queen_spider.lore: A black widow the size of a buckboard, crowned in bone. She climbs slow and spits silk at anything that shoots at her.
tips: Watch her spinnerets: when they glow white she's about to spit a web.
A webbed turret holds fire: shoot the white cocoon (three revolver shots) or wait 8 seconds.
She never webs more than three turrets at once.

burrow_beetle.lore: A shovel-headed digger that would rather go through your plateau than up your cliff.
tips: A trail of dust puffs shows where it is underground.
Cracks and an orange ring mark where it will burst up, three seconds early: the top level of every scaffold inside comes down.
Lantern light forces it up early, before it reaches your scaffolds.
It can only be hurt above ground, so be there when it surfaces.

tumble_titan.lore: A giant scarab that rolls a boulder bigger than a wagon up the wall, just to drop it on your house.
tips: The boulder shields it from shots from your lip, so shoot the boulder.
Mortars and dynamite near the boulder chip it too.
Cracked through, the boulder rolls back over the Titan: a third of its health in one go.
Reaching the top with it, the boulder flattens everything in a line across your plateau.

locust_lord.lore: A crowned locust that rules the swarm from the air, high over the canyon.
tips: His swarm sac glows before every cloud of six locusts.
Cliff turrets can't touch him: build anti-air, or shoot him yourself.
The locusts go for crops and water; down him and they stop coming.

acid_matriarch.lore: A scorpion queen carrying her brood, with an acid sac the size of a water barrel.
tips: She clings about halfway up and spits for half a minute before climbing on.
Her tail bulb swells green before every spit.
Acid eats a turret for 14 seconds unless a Water Cannon near it fires: each shot washes every turret around it.
A Water Cannon hit on her rinses out the spit she's winding up.

locust.lore: One of the Swarm Lord's locusts. One bite of corn and it's gone.
tips: Anti-air flak and shotguns clear the clouds.

hive_drone.lore: A stubby wasp shaken out of the Hive Wagon's hive.
tips: Splash and fire clear them as they climb.

mirage_mantis.lore: A praying mantis the colour of hot sand that only hunts inside a dust storm. She is always a shimmer of heat haze, and every few seconds she slips almost out of sight altogether.
tips: While she has faded, turrets lose her: keep shooting her yourself, you can still hit the ripple.
Build a lantern post near her climb: in its light she stays solid and every turret keeps firing.

hive_wagon.lore: A plated bug the size of a stagecoach, rolling on wheel-discs, with a paper wasp hive roped onto its back. Every hit stirs the hive up.
tips: While it's under fire it shakes out a burst of drones every couple of seconds, and a last swarm when it dies: kill it fast, with everything at once.
Splash turrets and fire patches clear the drones.

stilt_strider.lore: A harvestman slung between eight impossibly long legs. It holds its body far out from the wall and steps straight over the lip.
tips: Shoot its legs: every third broken leg drops it to the canyon floor.
A crippled Strider climbs slower and takes more damage. Turrets aim at its knees half the time.

thunder_cicada.lore: A hammer-headed cicada with amber drums on its sides. When it drums, the whole canyon hears it, and turrets in the ring are shaken senseless.
tips: Watch for the glowing ring on your plateau: everything inside is stunned for 4 seconds when the screech lands.
Spread your turrets out. It sits still while it drums: that's your moment to pour fire into it.

bone_collector.lore: A black-and-orange burying beetle with a cattle skull on its back. It eats the dead, and the more it eats the bigger it gets.
tips: It stops to feed on the corpse pile at the cliff foot: shoot the pile apart, or burn it with blasts and fire, before it gets there.
Bugs killed right beside it are a meal too: kill it before the swarm around it.

hive_queen.lore: The mother of the Hive, woken by the railroad's blast in 1889 and climbing out at last. A plated abdomen the size of a boxcar, a crest like a crown, and every bug in the canyon at her call.
tips: Her crown glows: it's her soft spot. Rifles and your own gun on the crown.
Her belly pulses before she calls a brood: splash and fire on the wall around her.
Amber resin gums a turret shut: shoot the cocoon free.
Hurt, she shrieks: every turret inside the ring is stunned. Spread them out.
Below a third she sheds her plates and climbs fast: everything you have, now.

hive_mother.lore: The Queen's mother, sealed in the lower hive since long before the railroad came, until the board blasted it open again. Blind, scarred, crusted with the amber the board would kill for, and bigger than anything that has climbed out of the canyon.
tips: Her old plates turn shots from the front: the amber geode on her brow is the soft spot.
Rings on your cliff mark where her amber hail lands: every turret near one is gummed shut. Spread out and shoot the cocoons free.
When she hums, her brood climbs faster: splash the wall around her.
Below a third her crust falls off and hatches hive drones: keep a sky gun ready.
She can't be buried by guns alone. Keep her on the wall.

gatling_post.lore: A hand-cranked gatling on a post. Shreds swarms, scratches armour.
tips: It can't dip below thirty degrees, so build it where it can see across the canyon.

buffalo_rifle.lore: A heavy rifle nest that puts a hole through anything.
tips: Pierces armour.

water_cannon.lore: Knocks climbers clean off the rock. Needs no ammo.
tips: The higher a bug is, the harder it falls.

chili_mortar.lore: Lobs flaming chili onto the cliff face. Burns chili as ammo.
tips: Great against packs climbing together.

dynamite_lobber.lore: Arcs dynamite for a big splash. Each stick costs 1 chitin from the team pot.
tips: Best on crowded lanes.

lasso_harpoon.lore: Pins one climber in place for a few seconds.
tips: Pair it with a Buffalo Rifle.

scattergun_post.lore: Last line: a brutal blast at bugs that reach your plateau.
tips: Never shoots cliff faces.

sharpshooter_tower.lore: Last line: a lookout with a long rifle over your yard.
tips: Never shoots cliff faces.

porch_repeater.lore: House turret: a quick twin gun on the porch, balcony or roof deck.
tips: Only shoots bugs near your house.

rooftop_cannon.lore: House turret: grapeshot that bursts over bugs at your door.
tips: Only shoots bugs near your house.

duck_gun.lore: A punt gun meant for a whole flock of ducks. Now it's for dragonflies.
tips: Air defence goes in the second row from the lip.
Slow but hits hard: good against a lone bandit.

sky_sweeper.lore: Two crank gatlings bolted together and pointed at the sky.
tips: Shoots any flier over either plateau or the canyon.
Weak per bullet; great against a swarm of bandits.

powder_flak.lore: Powder shells timed to burst in mid-air.
tips: Hits every flier in the burst.
Best where bandits bunch up over your farm.

net_thrower.lore: A spring arm that flings weighted nets.
tips: A netted flier hangs in the air for a few seconds.
Pair it with a Duck Gun or Sky Sweeper to finish them.

firework_battery.lore: A rack of skyrockets with very short fuses.
tips: Long range, big bursts, punches through armour.
Each rocket costs 1 chitin from the team pot.
Expensive: save it for blood moons.

big_bertha.lore: A ten-barrel crank Gatling bolted to a buckboard wagon. She wants a gunner: hold the trigger and she spins up and hoses the far wall until the barrels glow.
tips: Takes 2 x 2 of bare ground. Tap E to sit in her; the mouse aims, hold LMB to fire.
Let go before the barrels glow red: overheated, she's quiet until they cool.
Left alone she still fires, at half rate and half damage.

whaler.lore: A whaling ballista on a timber sledge. The barbed harpoon goes in on a chain and holds a big bug fast to the wall.
tips: LMB throws the harpoon; a chained bug stops climbing for a few seconds.
Hold RMB to reel it down the wall: the further you drag it, the harder it falls when the chain lets go.
Your answer to bosses and armoured beetles. Unmanned, it only harpoons big bugs.

thunder_mule.lore: Three stubby mortars on a mule cart. The mule doesn't care for the noise.
tips: Sitting in it shows the shells' arc and a landing ring on the far wall.
One pull lobs a three-shell salvo: aim at the crowd near the top.
Long reload, and the shells take a moment to land: lead the climb.

sky_hound.lore: Twin flak barrels on a sandbagged turntable. Every shell bursts in a black cloud.
tips: Shells burst beside the first flier near your aim, or where you aim.
The cloud keeps stinging anything that flies through it.
Turns almost all the way round: it covers your own sky too.

twin_gatling.lore: Two Gatlings yoked to one crank and a shared drum. Twice the lead of a Gatling Post.
tips: Still half damage on armour: pair it with a big-game gun.

hornets_nest.lore: A dozen barrels on a spinning drum. The shot rattles from one bug into the next.
tips: Each hit ricochets into up to two more bugs within 3 m: best on packed swarms.
Half damage on armour.

elephant_battery.lore: A double rifle built for elephants, bolted to a sledge. Each round goes clean through.
tips: Each round carries on into two more bugs in its line.
Pierces armour, +50% on heavy bugs.

rail_spike_driver.lore: A steam ram that drives a railroad spike between two rails. Slow, and nothing stops it.
tips: Skewers every climber in a line down the wall; the last one is pinned to the rock.
Aimed at the top bug, it takes the whole lane under it.

gatling_porch.lore: A Gatling bolted to the house. It covers the whole yard from the porch.
tips: Only fires at bugs on your plateau, never at cliffs.
Reaches the whole yard, not just the doorstep.

steam_cannon.lore: A coal-fired boiler bolted to a brass nozzle. Every blast is a cone of scalding steam: the highest climbers in it let go and fall, and everything left in the fog crawls.
tips: Knocks off up to three small climbers a blast, the highest first.
Heavy bugs only slip a little; bosses barely at all.
Pair it with a Gatling Post: slowed bugs are easy pickings.

flood_gate.lore: A dammed timber tank on the lip. It takes twenty seconds to fill, then throws the sluice and sends a flood down a whole lane of the far wall.
tips: Washes every small bug in a lane-wide band off the wall at once.
Heavy bugs slip a few metres; bosses hardly budge.
Best on a lane the bugs crowd into.

twin_mortar.lore: Two tubes on one carriage. Each salvo drops a blast shell on the pack and a chili fire shell just above it, so whatever lives through the bang climbs into the flames.
tips: Eats a chili and a chitin every salvo.
Slow shells: fast bugs are gone before they land.
Can't touch fliers.

bola_launcher.lore: A spring gun with a revolving drum of bolas. Each throw wraps two climbers in weighted rope and holds them where they cling.
tips: Tangles two bugs at once; almost no damage.
Hold a heavy bug in a Buffalo Rifle's sights.
Bosses shake it off after a second.

cotton_bale_cannon.lore: A stubby cannon that fires a whole roped cotton bale. It bursts on the wall into a mat of rope and lint that holds four climbers where they cling.
tips: Crop-fed: it fires only after you load it with a cotton load (E), and the load lasts one wave.
Steps up from a Bola Launcher (Y): tangles four bugs at once and holds them longer.
Almost no damage. Bosses shake it off after a second.

amber_kiln.lore: A squat brick furnace mortar from the railroad's own smelting sheds, fed hive amber instead of coal. It lobs gobbets of molten resin that set harder than iron in seconds: anything it leaves below half health is sealed on the wall as an amber statue.
tips: Statues block the climb: bugs behind one must step round it or stall. Bosses aren't entombed, only slowed while the amber sets.
Any other hit (your guns, other turrets' blasts) shatters a statue for a little chitin for the team pot. The amber turrets' own shots never break one.
A statue crumbles by itself after about 24 s, and the bug inside dies with it.
Craft it at your Workshop's Amber tab: 10 hive amber, a Tripod mount, a Cannon barrel and a Fire load. The team fields only one.

queens_bell.lore: A great bell of cast hive amber in a gilded frame, struck by a steam hammer. The hive hears its queen in the note: every toll sets the ordinary bugs on the far wall upon each other and shakes fliers out of the sky.
tips: Tolls every 9 s whenever anything's in reach: bugs in range bite their neighbours for 6 s instead of climbing.
Fliers in range drop: the fall hurts, and any that live lie stunned. Bosses are only stunned for 2 s a toll.
Still bound by the thirty-degree law: it reaches only the part of the wall a turret could aim at.
Craft it at your Workshop's Amber tab: 12 hive amber, a Post mount, a Nozzle barrel and an Explosive load. The team fields only one.

mandible_lance.lore: A heat lance on a rail carriage. Its emitter is a queen's mandible cut from the Iron Mandible wreck, and it burns amber from a glass tank: one continuous beam that reaches the whole of the far wall and cuts through everything in its way.
tips: Everything in the beam's spot or along its line burns, armour or not. Where the beam drags from bug to bug it leaves a burning trail.
8 s of fire overheats it; it vents steam for 10 s. Idle, it cools off.
Craft it at your Workshop's Amber tab: 14 hive amber, a Tripod mount, a Rifle barrel and an Acid load. The team fields only one.

repeater_post.lore: A beefed-up gatling: thicker barrel shroud, brass cooling fins, twin belts. Tighter and faster than the Gatling Post.
tips: Self-powered: it fires every wave without any crop.

brass_gatling.lore: Six polished brass barrels with steam vents. The strongest gun that never needs a crop.
tips: Self-powered: it fires every wave without any crop.

long_tom_rifle.lore: An absurdly long rifle on an iron tripod with a brass telescope. The longest reach in the canyon.
tips: Self-powered: it fires every wave without any crop.

big_fifty.lore: A heavy .50 buffalo gun on a timber crutch with a buckhorn sight. Bigger slugs and a longer reach than the Buffalo Rifle, the step between it and the Long Tom.
tips: Self-powered: it fires every wave without any crop.
Steps up from a Buffalo Rifle (Y) and on to a Long Tom Rifle.
Best on big and armoured bugs.

buck_blaster.lore: Last line: a sawed-off double barrel on a swivel. Brutal on bugs that reach your plateau.
tips: Self-powered: it fires every wave without any crop.

grapeshot_turret.lore: Last line: a naval carronade loaded with grapeshot. One blast clears a patch of your plateau.
tips: Self-powered: it fires every wave without any crop.

skeet_post.lore: An upward-angled rifle on a tall swivel with brass tracking gears. Follows fast fliers.
tips: Self-powered: it fires every wave without any crop.

flak_porch.lore: A wide-bore flak cannon: shells burst in the air and pepper every flier in the cloud.
tips: Self-powered: it fires every wave without any crop.

corn_hopper.lore: A tin hopper of dried corn feeds a rapid-fire barrel. Hits harder than a Gatling Post while it has corn.
tips: Crop-fed: it fires only after you load it with a corn load (E), and the load lasts one wave.

twin_hopper.lore: Two corn hoppers on one swivel: twin barrels, double the fire rate.
tips: Crop-fed: it fires only after you load it with a corn load (E), and the load lasts one wave.

pepper_sprayer.lore: Leather bellows blast a cloud of ground chili down the wall. Leaves a wide burning patch.
tips: Crop-fed: it fires only after you load it with a chili load (E), and the load lasts one wave.

sulfur_fume_vent.lore: A chimney burning sulfur root. Rolls a toxic yellow cloud over the lip of the far wall.
tips: Crop-fed: it fires only after you load it with a sulfur root load (E), and the load lasts one wave.

brimstone_bellows.lore: A brick firebox and a great leather bellows. Every pump drives a long plume of burning sulfur far down the far wall.
tips: Crop-fed: it fires only after you load it with a sulfur root load (E), and the load lasts one wave.
Steps up from a Sulfur Fume Vent (Y): a wider, longer-lasting cloud.
Little punch on armour: pair it with a rifle.

herb_rifle.lore: A long rifle firing herb-acid tipped rounds that eat through armour.
tips: Crop-fed: it fires only after you load it with a herbs load (E), and the load lasts one wave.

tripwire_fence.lore: Last line: tumbleweed wire strung low across your yard. Snares a bug that reaches your plateau for 3 s.
tips: Crop-fed: it fires only after you load it with a tumbleweed vine load (E), and the load lasts one wave.

bramble_bomb.lore: Last line: a thorny tumbleweed ball rigged with dynamite. Bursts into brambles that pin and burn bugs on your plateau.
tips: Crop-fed: it fires only after you load it with a tumbleweed vine load (E), and the load lasts one wave.

dust_devil_trap.lore: Last line: whips tumbleweed into a little tornado that flings bugs off your plateau.
tips: Crop-fed: it fires only after you load it with a tumbleweed vine load (E), and the load lasts one wave.

siege_mortar.lore: A massive iron mortar firing barrel cactus shells. The biggest single hit in the canyon.
tips: Crop-fed: it fires only after you load it with a barrel cactus load (E), and the load lasts one wave.

corn.lore: Sweet canyon corn. Grows like a weed and keeps a rancher fed.
tips: Each harvest gives 4 loads for the Corn Hopper line, plus a little to keep.
Plant it between waves for quick chitin for the team pot at the market.
Left click with corn out to eat it when your belly growls.

prickly_pear.lore: A stubborn cactus fruit. Takes its time, but it's food, water and medicine in one.
tips: Each harvest gives 2 loads for the Water Cannon line, plus a little to keep.
Eating a pear heals a little and quenches thirst.
The pads give back more water than they drink.

firecracker_chili.lore: Hot enough to light a fuse. The Chili Mortar won't fire without it.
tips: Each harvest gives 3 loads for the Chili Mortar line, plus a little to keep.
Keep a stock before building a Chili Mortar: every shot burns one.
The market pays your own scrap for chilies, the only crop that does.

herbs.lore: Desert sage, dried and bundled. Better than any snake-oil tonic.
tips: Each harvest gives 2 loads for the Herb Rifle line, plus a little to keep.
Carry a few into every wave: a dose heals 50 HP.
Herbs fetch the most chitin per unit at the market.

sarsaparilla.lore: A twining vine with heart-shaped leaves and a thick, knobbly root that brews the canyon's best tonic. You don't grow it for yourself: you grow it for whoever is guarding your wall.
tips: Each harvest gives 2 loads for the crewed guns, plus a little to keep.
Hold a root (hotbar 4) and left click to send your partner a tonic: their turrets fire 15% faster.
Each tonic adds 60 s, stacking up to 3 minutes. The clock only runs during a wave, so send them any time.
Can't use it yourself? Store roots in your partner's deposit box and let them brew for you.
The market won't buy it. Seeds are at the airship market.

cotton.lore: Soft canyon cotton, braided into ropes, bolas and nets.
tips: Each harvest gives 3 loads for the Lasso Harpoon line.

sulfur_root.lore: A gnarly yellow root that smells like a struck match.
tips: Thirsty and slow, but each harvest gives 2 loads for the Dynamite Lobber line.

barrel_cactus.lore: A squat ribbed cactus that never needs watering.
tips: Plant it and forget it: one load for the Siege Mortar.

tumbleweed_vine.lore: A fast vine that balls up into tumbleweeds.
tips: Each harvest gives 4 loads for the Tripwire Fence line.

thirty_degree_law.title: The Thirty-Degree Law
thirty_degree_law.lore: Territorial Board of Firearms, 1871: no barrel shall dip more than thirty degrees beneath the horizon. Everybody knows why. On the 4th of July, 1871, Governor Horace Pell fired down from the rim of Dry Gulch at a rattlesnake and shot three of his own toes off. 'If a Governor cannot shoot downhill safely, no man can,' said Chairman Vane of the Western Plains & Pacific, and the law passed by spring. Settlers call it Pell's Toes.
tips: No turret or gun can aim more than 30 degrees down.
Nothing on the rim can shoot down to the canyon floor either. Ride down the rope to deal with anything down there.

team_scrap.title: Chitin: The Team Pot
team_scrap.lore: Chitin is shared: bug pieces, and every bug pays in. Everyone builds turrets, scaffolds, farm plots and house repairs from one team pot, and every kill, shell heap, town bounty and crop sale pays back into it.
tips: The Team Chitin counter (bottom left) is the same number on every screen.
Talk it over before a big build: it's everyone's chitin.
Breaching bugs steal from the pot, so keep them off the plateau.
A CPU teammate only ever spends its fair share of the team's chitin.

your_chitin.title: Scrap: Yours Alone
your_chitin.lore: Scrap is personal. It pays for your own guns, gun mods, turret upgrades and house upgrades, and comes from the junk heap by your house (salvage it every build phase; it pays more as the waves grow), chilies sold at the market, railroad wrecks on the canyon floor and the casino.
tips: Your Scrap (bottom left) is only yours: your partner can't spend it.
Water, crops, seeds, parts and crafted turrets are personal too.

grow_for_partner.title: Grow for Your Partner
grow_for_partner.lore: Sarsaparilla Root grows for the other cliff: you grow it, and it makes THEIR turrets fire faster.
tips: Left click with a root out to send a tonic.
A green line under your health shows a tonic on your turrets, or yours on theirs.

lucky_moreau.title: Lucky Moreau, the Fence
lucky_moreau.lore: A gambler in a black duster with a booth by the airship's starboard rail. "I hear the railroad lost a strongbox. Got anything shiny?" He deals only in hive amber.
tips: He comes aboard once the story is past chapter 4, or from wave 8 in a normal run.
Sells Lucky's finish on the gunsmith's irons (they keep their level and mods), an exclusive wardrobe look, one-night favours (a supply drop, a bounty top-up) and the three amber turret blueprints.
Blueprints you buy or find are yours for good: the team can craft that turret in any run you ride in.

grapple_dynamite.title: The Grapple's Dynamite
grapple_dynamite.lore: The gunsmith's Powder Satchel: a bundle of three sticks, twine and a fuse in your free hand, and a match strip riveted down the grapple launcher. Strike it, throw it, cover your ears. Pell's Toes says no barrel shall dip below thirty degrees; it says nothing about a man's arm.
grapple_dynamite.stats: 50 scrap at the gunsmith (Upgrades)  ·  160 damage in 6.5 m, less at the edge  ·  3 bundles, one back every 40 s up top
tips: Grapple out (0), then R raises a bundle and R again strikes and throws it. It lands where you aim, out to 60 m, far enough for the far wall.
Fuse lit means it's going: switching away won't put it out.
It cracks armour, and a climber that lives through it is shaken on its line.
It blows teammates off their feet but never hurts them, and leaves the turrets be.
The loudest thing in the canyon: on the floor it wakes every sleeper for 150 m and brings them running.
Modifications: Bigger Blast, Heavier Charge, and Coal Oil to set the survivors burning.

mouth.lore: Where a bug tunnel opens onto the canyon floor, behind old mine shoring somebody nailed up years back. Shed husks and chitin for the team pot, the odd turret part, and pages Doc Whitlow dropped on his way in.
tips: A few mites sleep in heaps here. Walk soft: they wake if you get close.
Gunfire carries. Every sleeper nearby comes to see who rang the bell.

boneyard.lore: The bleached carcass of something enormous, ribs arching out of the sand. Scavenger beetles pick it over, and the rarest turret parts turn up between the bones.
tips: You can walk in under the ribcage.
The boss trophy carries an upgrade token on its horn.

camp.lore: A railroad survey crew left in a hurry: tents still pitched, the theodolite still level, supper still on the fire. Their crates hold blueprints, Doc's specimen jars and journal pages.
tips: They booby-trapped the place: bear traps in the grass and a dynamite tripwire between the tents.
Look at a trap and press E to disarm it.

nest.lore: A crater of resin and mud full of humming eggs, glowing green in the dark. Brood guards and spiders sleep round the rim.
tips: E takes a clutch of eggs to sell at the airship market.
F smashes a clutch. Smash most of them and that tunnel sends a fifth fewer bugs next wave. Smashing is loud.

wreck.lore: Number Seven came off the trestle in '89 and nobody ever hauled her out. Her cars are full of scrap: cartloads of it, more than a night on the cliff pays.
tips: The wreck creaks when it starts to give. When it creaks, leave: timbers come down soon after.
Once it collapses, the rest of the scrap is buried until the next refill.

egg.lore: A clutch of bug eggs, warm and humming. Sells for team chitin at the airship market (the price drops as you sell).
tips: Or smash them at the nest to thin that tunnel's next wave.

specimen.lore: A glass jar with something curled up and glowing inside. Doc Whitlow pays scrap for them through the airship market.

journal_page.lore: Loose pages of Doc Whitlow's field journal, blown into the tunnel mouths and left at the survey camp.
tips: Each page you pick up reads out a line from the journal.

amber.lore: Hive amber: the resin the bugs build their nests from, set into glowing honey-gold lumps. It burns hotter than coal and sets harder than iron, and the railroad's board has been mining it in secret since '89.
tips: Found only on the canyon floor: a few chips at some raid sites after each refill, more at bug nests and railroad wrecks.
Heavy: 4 backpack weight a chip. Yours alone, like scrap (never the team pot).
Lucky Moreau on the airship takes nothing else; the amber turrets are made of it.
